candidates.name: Uveitis
support_spans: 2+ fine keratic precipitates, and 1+ cells in the anterior chamber
candidates.why: The patient's history of recurrent iritis and current symptoms of conjunctival injection and keratic precipitates suggest uveitis.

candidates.name: Cystoid macular edema
support_spans: cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye
OCT: Right eye showed significant cystoid macular edema and subfoveal fluid
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging results indicate cystoid macular edema.

candidates.name: Sarcoidosis
contradict_spans: Tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders were within reference limits
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of bilateral iritis and cystoid macular edema could be related to sarcoidosis, although the blood tests did not support this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis-associated uveitis
contradict_spans: The patient is 65 years old, which is not typical for juvenile idiopathic arthritis
candidates.why: The patient's history of recurrent bilateral iritis could suggest a diagnosis of juvenile idiopathic arthritis-associated uveitis, although the patient's age is not typical for this condition.

candidates.name: Diabetic macular edema
support_spans: cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye
contradict_spans: The patient's medical history and past medication use were otherwise unremarkable, with no mention of diabetes
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of cystoid macular edema could be related to diabetic macular edema, although there is no mention of diabetes in the patient's medical history.

candidates.name: Posterior scleritis
contradict_spans: No inflammation in the periphery was noted in either eye
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of cystoid macular edema and epiretinal membrane could suggest a diagnosis of posterior scleritis, although the lack of peripheral inflammation does not support this diagnosis.
